title: Trent on scripture
hook: the council confirms the full canon, and scripture with tradition

segments.voice: Yesterday, the Catholic Reformation began at Trent. Your line was reform from within. Did your one habit get its first step? Day seven hundred eighty-five.

"But the souls of the just are in the hand of God, and the torment of death shall not touch them." It's among the readings the Church offers for funerals. It comes from the Book of Wisdom. Open some Bibles and you won't find it at all. Open others and it's there, in a section set apart. Open a Catholic Bible and it sits among the other books, no fence around it. Which books belong in the Bible was one of the reformers' questions, and Trent answered it early. Today's title is Trent on scripture.
screen: `A FUNERAL READING.` → `IN SOME BIBLES, NOT OTHERS.` → `TRENT ANSWERS EARLY.`

segments.voice: First, the list. The council didn't just say the Bible matters. It wrote out the books by name, one after another, so nobody could wonder. In that list, among the others, are Tobias, Judith, Wisdom, Ecclesiasticus, also called Sirach, Baruch, and the books of the Maccabees. Catholics call these the deuterocanonical books. The decree speaks of them as books the Church was accustomed to read; Trent made the list official and binding. Next, scripture with tradition. The decree says the truth and discipline of the Gospel are found in the written books and in the unwritten traditions that came from Christ through the apostles. The council said it receives both with the same reverence. Not the Bible versus the Church, but the Bible read inside a living Church. Then, where others stand, without ranking. Protestant traditions call these same books the Apocrypha. Some Protestant Bibles print them in a separate section, as useful reading; others leave them out. Orthodox Bibles include them as well. The disagreement is real, and it's an honest one about how the early Church read. Last, the Latin. Trent also named the old Latin Bible, the Vulgate, as the authentic text for public reading and teaching, and called for it to be carefully printed. For Catholics, the council's point was to name every book the Church reads, each one in full standing: the whole canon.
screen: `THE BOOKS LISTED BY NAME.` · `SCRIPTURE AND TRADITION, TOGETHER.` · `OTHER CHURCHES, OTHER LISTS.` · `THE VULGATE NAMED AUTHENTIC.` · then, large: `THE WHOLE CANON.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: read from a deuterocanonical book. If you have a Catholic Bible, open to Wisdom, chapter three, or to Sirach, or Tobias, and read a few verses slowly, out loud if you can. If you don't have one nearby, stay with today's line from Wisdom: the souls of the just are in the hand of God. Say it once, then sit with it. Let one name come to mind, someone you've lost. If you pray, you can place them, in your mind, in that hand. The bell holds the time.
Vulgate. The old Latin Bible that Trent named as the Church's authentic text, standing alongside the full list of books it declared canonical. Today's word.
Your line: the whole canon. Today, read one passage from a part of the Bible you usually skip, and let it count. Day seven hundred eighty-five.

howItsDone: Catholic Bibles print the deuterocanonical books among the others, and readings from them, like Wisdom 3 at funerals, are part of the Mass lectionary.

notes: The index hook says '73-book canon'; the decree lists books by name without a total, so under the claims rule the count is not spoken. Keeper may wish to add it.
Douay-Rheims book names used (Tobias, Ecclesiasticus); Trent's list also includes Baruch and 1–2 Maccabees. Confirm the names given.
'They had been read in the Church long before' (e.g. earlier lists at Florence and regional councils): confirm.
Scripture and tradition 'with the same reverence' paraphrases 'pari pietatis affectu ac reverentia'; confirm.
Protestant and Orthodox positions described briefly without ranking; Orthodox canons vary and include some further books. Confirm phrasing.
Wisdom 3:1 at Catholic funerals (lectionary option): confirm.
'Deuterocanonical' used as the Catholic term; its etymology is deliberately not taught under the claims rule.
Editor: tied 'read in the Church long before' to the decree's own wording instead of an outside historical claim.
Editor 2: varied the teach's closing line.
Audit: closing 'the whole story, not a shortened one' cut, since it framed other churches' Bibles as shortened right after promising no ranking.
